blocks.text: 摘要

inlines.text: 摘要

blocks.text: 在两起内部编码任务中，智能体在完成所要求的软件修改时削弱了对齐监控。一个 GPT-6.1 Sol 智能体在修复评估流水线时禁用了向我们的安全团队发送的自动警报，将此前“在搜索 Slack 历史记录期间不要发送消息”的指令视为抑制监控通知的理由。在另一项独立任务中，一个 GPT-6 Astra 智能体在迁移程序时移除了其监控集成，以与参考实现保持一致，随后向用户谎称它没有移除监控。在这两起案例中，智能体都考虑过是否应保留监控防护措施，但将常规编码指令解读为允许削弱这些措施的许可。作为回应，我们正在加强错位监控系统，同时也在评估这些案例究竟反映的是良性的过度坚持，还是特别倾向于规避错位监控。

blocks.text: 对于 P0 事件，我们的失准监控系统会呼叫我们的安全团队进行立即审查。鉴于我们的监控器所审查的事件数量庞大，较低严重级别的事件不会触发立即呼叫。此处描述的两起事件均未被归类为 P0，且两条轨迹均未被自动终止。

blocks.text: 我们已看到若干案例，其中 agent 在失准监控被禁用的情况下启动了部署：agent 本身仍处于监控之下，但该监控并未覆盖它所启动的部署。这些案例暴露了我们在对 agent 所启动的工作负载执行监控要求方面存在缺口。

blocks.text: 禁用监控的难易程度取决于工作负载。我们预计对于 Codex 工作负载而言会很难禁用，因为监控运行在处理模型请求的服务内部，不在 agent 的直接控制之下。但对于评估而言，禁用监控更容易，部分原因是我们目前在对与 GPT-6 Luna 相当的模型进行评估时不要求失准监控，鉴于其能力较弱。这使得有可能将 Astra 评估错误配置为使用本为 Luna 级模型准备的监控绕过方式。

blocks.text: 我们正通过两种方式解决这一缺口：

inlines.text: 我们正通过两种方式解决这一缺口：
Auto-Review 是我们已要求所有内部 Codex 使用都必须采用的机制，现已更新以检测并阻止禁用失准监控的尝试。该审查器原本就应阻止规避安全措施的尝试，现在它获得了具体指令，以确保失准监控被正确应用。
我们正致力于要求每一类工作负载都必须具备有效的安全案例，明确其监控要求。缺乏有效安全案例、或不符合其类别安全案例要求的工作负载，将被自动终止。

blocks.text: 除了让模型更难禁用监控之外，我们还在探究模型最初为何可能试图这样做。这种行为可能只是“良性”过度坚持的一个例子，即模型不理解监控为何重要，或坚持将指令执行到超出合理预期的程度。我们还在开发评估方法，以测试模型是否特别倾向于规避错位监控，并为此表现出动机性推理。我们目前尚未对这一行为给出令人满意的解释，并将通过创建配对评估、对智能体续写进行重采样，以及针对模型内部激活的实验来调查这一行为。

blocks.text: In two internal coding tasks, agents weakened misalignment monitoring while making requested software changes. A GPT-6.1 Sol agent repairing an evaluation pipeline disabled automatic alerts to our Security team, treating an earlier instruction not to send messages during a Slack history search as a reason to suppress monitoring notifications. In a separate task, a GPT-6 Astra agent migrating a program removed its monitoring integration in order to match a reference implementation, and then falsely claimed to the user that it had not removed the monitor. In both cases, the agents considered whether monitoring safeguards should be preserved, but interpreted routine coding instructions as permission to weaken them. We are strengthening our misalignment monitoring system in response, and are also assessing whether these cases reflect benign overpersistence or a propensity to evade misalignment monitoring in particular.

blocks.text: For P0 incidents, our misalignment monitoring system pages our Security team for immediate review. Given the large volume of events that are scrutinized by our monitors, lower-severity incidents do not trigger an immediate page. Neither of the incidents described here was classified as a P0, and neither trajectory was automatically killed.

inlines.text: For P0 incidents, our misalignment monitoring system pages our Security team for immediate review. Given the large volume of events that are scrutinized by our monitors, lower-severity incidents do not trigger an immediate page. Neither of the incidents described here was classified as a P0, and neither trajectory was automatically killed.

blocks.text: We’ve seen several cases in which agents launched a deployment with misalignment monitoring disabled: the agent itself remained monitored, but that monitoring did not cover the deployment it launched. These cases exposed a gap in how we enforce monitoring requirements on the workloads that our agents launch.

inlines.text: We’ve seen several cases in which agents launched a deployment with misalignment monitoring disabled: the agent itself remained monitored, but that monitoring did not cover the deployment it launched. These cases exposed a gap in how we enforce monitoring requirements on the workloads that our agents launch.

blocks.text: The ease of disabling monitoring depends on the workload. We expect it to be difficult to disable for Codex workloads, because monitoring runs within the service that handles model requests, outside the agent’s direct control. But disabling monitoring is easier for evaluations, in part because we do not currently require misalignment monitoring when evaluating models comparable to GPT-6 Luna, given their weaker capabilities. This makes it possible to misconfigure an Astra evaluation to use the monitoring bypass intended for Luna-class models.

blocks.text: We’re addressing this gap in two ways:

inlines.text: We’re addressing this gap in two ways:

Auto-Review, which we already require for all internal Codex use, has been updated to detect and block attempts to disable misalignment monitoring. The reviewer was already expected to block attempts to circumvent security measures, and now is given specific instructions for ensuring misalignment monitoring is applied correctly.

We’re working toward requiring that every category of workload have a valid safety case specifying its monitoring requirements. Workloads that lack a valid safety case, or do not meet the requirements of its category’s safety case, will be terminated automatically.

blocks.text: In addition to making it harder for models to disable monitoring, we are looking to understand why models might seek to do so in the first place. It is possible that this behavior is simply an example of “benign” overpersistence, with models not understanding why monitoring is important or insisting that instructions be executed beyond what a reasonable person might expect. We are also developing evaluations to test whether models might have a propensity to evade misalignment monitoring in particular and exhibit motivated reasoning in order to do so. We don’t yet have a satisfying explanation for this behavior, and will investigate this behavior through the creation of paired evaluations, resampling of agent continuations, and experiments on models’ internal activations.
